change: No changes. Primary (Gluteus Maximus + Gluteus Medius) and secondary (Hamstrings, Lower Back, abs) confirmed correct. EMG research confirms single-leg banded glute bridge produces high gluteus activation; Gluteus Medius is well-engaged due to unilateral load and band tension above knees forcing hip abductor activation. Core (abs) and hamstrings as stabilizers are well-supported.

No changes. Primary (Gluteus Maximus) and secondary (Hamstrings, Lower Back) confirmed correct. Hip extension kickback in bent-over position isolates Gluteus Maximus; Hamstrings assist in hip extension; Erector Spinae stabilizes the hinge position. Gluteus Medius not included as primary — it is an abductor and not a prime mover in straight-leg kickback.

Added 'Lower Traps' to primary mid back latins (was: Rhomboids, Upper Traps; now: Rhomboids, Upper Traps, Lower Traps). EMG study (Fukunaga et al., IJSPT) and multiple sources confirm lower trapezius is meaningfully active during band pull-apart, preventing scapular anterior tipping. Lower Traps omission was an error. All other data retained.

Moved Hamstrings from secondary to primary, and made all three posterior chain muscles (Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings, Lower Back/Erector Spinae) primary movers. Multiple sources including EMG research confirm that in reverse hyperextensions, glutes, hamstrings, and erector spinae are all prime movers — not stabilizers. Hamstrings co-extend the hip alongside glutes. Abs retained as secondary (core stabilization on bench). Original data incorrectly had Hamstrings as secondary only.

Added Gluteus Maximus to secondary (moved before Abductor entry). Research confirms Gluteus Maximus acts as a stabilizer during seated hip abduction with superior fibers assisting abduction. Primary (Gluteus Medius) unchanged. Abductor (TFL) retained as secondary. Original secondary only had Abductor — Gluteus Maximus stabilizer role was missing.
